goal: Create an independent designer plan to refactor DeerFlow from chat-oriented interaction into a workspace/project-oriented AI plant-breeding operating system with human coworkers, GreenAgent-gated DBTL agents, durable database records, and a provenance-aware knowledge base.
acceptance_criteria: The two Designer plans are consolidated under plan/design; current code constraints are cited; the database-authoritative reconciliation contract, PostgreSQL production boundary, global Inbox, maize-first generic schema, strict knowledge promotion, hypotheses, minority positions, tester requirements, human gates, target architecture, migration constraints, and acceptance criteria are explicit; no implementation or research files are modified.

test_human_review_decision.summary: Route the stale acceptance contract back to Designer and redefine this delivery as a narrower foundation demonstration. New UI direction: project-focused left sidebar (projects as folders), chat exists only inside a project (no independent chat), no DBTL integration this cycle, minimum reviewable result for human comments.

rescoped_acceptance_criteria: A project owns a durable workspace directory that every conversation in it reads and writes through the sandbox.
Conversation membership is a durable threads_meta scope row written through an authorized endpoint, not chat metadata.
A project's files and conversations are addressable by project id with no conversation open.
The run's owning project is server-derived and any client-supplied value is stripped.
Uploads remain conversation-scoped, and unfiled conversations keep their own workspace.
Backend TDD tests, lint/format, frontend checks and tests all pass.

comments: Sidebar had duplicate project folders; simplify and keep the design concise.
Adopt the Biomni-style second rail: Tasks as DBTL Cycles, Drive as a per-cycle To-Do list; be creative.
The Biomni third rail is where chat renders.
Legacy projectless conversations route to /workspace/chats.
DBTL integration remains deferred.
Remove the /workspace/projects route and the portfolio icon on the sidebar group label; add a + action to create projects instead.
Put the project name directly after /workspace/ instead of /workspace/projects/project-<uuid>.
Opening a project must land directly in chat, not on a project brief page.
Clicking the project name should display its subfolders; the Files folder can be associated there and removed from the top tab.
Display the agents working on this project (placeholder for now; more agents come later).
Minimize the Cycles section when no active cycle is running.
Scope files to a project, not a thread — or associate the thread with the project.
The whole refactor is around a project, not chat; this makes later changes clearer.
Move uploads to the project too (both halves).
Sandbox providers explained; container/VM project mounts implemented later.
Field report: G2F conversation hit sandbox denials and the project folder tree stayed empty.
A project should be a folder the user owns in the local filesystem (e.g. ~/Documents/projects/G2F), human-accessible — not an internal sandbox tree.
New chat still not as expected: agent claims it cannot see the local filesystem and offers terminal commands.
Clicking G2F in the sidebar starts a new chat instead of displaying subdirectories.
The agent still does not find the correct path for the project (sibling folder greenagent-test).
It says it cannot write directly — allow it to do so.

known_limitations: Project slug is resolved client-side; backend by-slug lookup and per-workspace uniqueness still pending.
Only LocalSandboxProvider implements project-owned storage; AIO/E2B/BoxLite accept and ignore project_id (deferred per human answer #2).
